title: Family, cousin Joe Baptiste, and uptown Carrollton
summary: No musicians in his family except a banjo-playing cousin, Joe Baptiste; they talk about Carrollton and the horse and mule cars.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Adams, way uptown. Almost Carlton, is that? That's Carlton, yes. I wonder if you could tell us anything about your family, if your father, mother, any uncles, anybody played music in your family when you were a child? Do you remember any music in your home?
No. No. I had a cousin that played banjo.
What was his name? Joe Baptiste. Oh, Joe Baptiste. I think I've heard him. I know I've heard some of the Baptiste's names before. Uh-huh. Was he older than you, I guess?
Oh, yeah. He's older than me. Did he play with any bands? Do you remember? Yeah, he was playing with different bands, but by me being so small, I mean I wouldn't know the names of the bands. Yeah.
And your father didn't play any instrument? No.
No, my father didn't. In fact, nobody in my family but him at that time. Yeah.

And you were a boy, you remember, up in Carlton, was it all connected right to the city, or was it seemed like another little town up the river? No, it was all connected. All connected to those days. I know at one time they even ran a little railroad up there, you know, a separate town. Yeah.
Well, I was born during the time of the mule cars, but I mean it still was horse cars, they called them at that time.
Yeah, that was by the city.
